> **If they didn't laugh, it wouldn't be the Dao.**

"If the people hearing it didn't laugh, then what was said isn't the Dao."

Sounds arrogant — but really it means: **the Dao inherently exceeds most people's cognitive framework**. People hearing it laugh, because they try to measure it with their own framework, can't, and laugh.

This is very modern-product-like —

---

You ship a product. It might be great, but it will **almost certainly** be heard by three kinds of people:

- **The higher** — they hear, use it quietly, send feedback quietly, you **may not even hear from them**
- **The middling** — they hear, say "interesting, but can't quite say"
- **The lower** — they hear, laugh out loud, "that's it? that's all?"

Laozi doesn't say the higher are "above" — he **describes** three responses.

**The point is the last line**: "The lower person hearing the Dao, laughs out loud" — the lower laugh because the Dao is the opposite of the "yes/no" they know.

---

Next Laozi lists a set of **"reverse definitions"**:

| Surface | Actual |
|---|---|
| Bright Dao seems dark | the truly clear-headed looks "confused" |
| Advancing Dao seems retreating | the truly advancing looks "falling back" |
| Level Dao seems uneven | the truly level road looks "bumpy" |
| Highest virtue seems a valley | the truly virtuous looks "empty" |
| Purest white seems stained | the truly "white" (innocent) looks "insulted" |
| Widest virtue seems insufficient | the truly "wide" virtue looks "not enough" |
| Most solid virtue seems lazy | the truly "building" virtue looks "slacking" |
| Truest substance seems muddied | the truly "plain" looks "turbid" |
| Greatest square has no corners | the truly "great" square has **no edges** (no rules) |
| Greatest vessel completes latest | the truly "great" vessel **completes latest** (can't be rushed) |
| Greatest sound is rarely heard | the truly "great" sound is **silent** (no roar) |
| Greatest image has no form | the truly "great" image **has no shape** |

**This set of reverse definitions says: "great" things don't look "great"**.

You build a product, the truly great product **doesn't look great** — it's like a tool, like water, like air, you don't think of it as "great".

WeChat is not "great". Alipay is not "great". Google Search is not "great" — they **work so well you forget they exist**.

**This is "the greatest image has no form"**.

---

The last line lands softly:

> **The Dao is hidden, nameless. And yet, only the Dao, generously lends and completes.**

"The Dao" is hidden, has no name. **But "the Dao" is generous** — it "lends" you things, and **completes** (fulfills) you.

"Generously lends and completes" — **the Dao completes you**, as long as you're willing to take it.
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"下士闻道,大笑之"读成"老子瞧不起普通老百姓"。

**错的。**

老子没说"下士低"——老子说"**下士笑"**。这是描述反应,不是评判人。

"下士"是**用现有框架在测"道"的人**——他们的框架够用,但道的形状超出他们的框架,所以他们笑。

**你身边那个"看一眼就喷"的同事,他不是坏——他是在用他仅有的尺子量世界**。尺子不够长,显得东西很怪。

**反方的真问题是**: 你打算**让他把你的东西"测"成什么样**?如果他的尺子量你量出来是"怪",你**该高兴**——因为真道都怪。

**大器晚成**也是——这 4 个字经常被人读成"成功要熬",但老子的本意是**"大器"不可能被强推快成**。你催,反而催不出大器。
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "the lower person hearing the Dao laughs out loud" as "Laozi looks down on ordinary folks".

**Wrong.**

Laozi didn't say the lower are "below" — Laozi said "**the lower laugh**". This describes a response, not a judgment of people.

"The lower" are **people who try to measure the Dao with their existing framework** — their framework is sufficient, but the Dao's shape exceeds their framework, so they laugh.

**That colleague of yours who scans once and flames** — he's not bad — he's using his only ruler to measure the world. The ruler isn't long enough, the thing looks weird.

**The real counter-question is**: what are you going to **let his measurement make of you**? If his ruler measures you as "weird" — you **should be happy** — because the real Dao is always weird.

**"Great vessel completes latest"** is similar — these 4 words are often read as "success takes time", but Laozi's actual meaning is **a "great vessel" cannot be rushed into completion**. You push, and you push out a non-great vessel.
chapters.scene_cn:
你做了一个新产品——你团队熬了 3 个月。

上线第二天,社交媒体上几条评论:

- "**这玩意儿是给谁用的?**" (下士大笑)
- "**看着还行,但好像也没啥特别的**" (中士若存若亡)
- "**我用了一周,确实省了我 30 分钟/天**" (上士勤而行之)

你盯着这三条评论,心里不舒服——因为被嘲笑的那条最显眼,转发最多。

**老子会说: 被笑不等于产品失败**。

你那 1000 个"上士"用户——他们**没在社交媒体上夸你**,他们**在默默用**。他们不会发"我今天用 X 省了 30 分钟",因为这种事太小了,小到不值得发。

你看到的"嘲笑"——是下士在用自己"懂"的东西去测"他不懂的东西",测不出来,所以笑。

**产品真正的成功,不在于"上线后没被笑",而在于"上线后有人默默用了一周"**。
chapters.scene_en:
You shipped a new product — your team worked 3 months.

Day 2 after launch, some comments on social media:

- "**Who is this for?**" (the lower laugh out loud)
- "**Looks fine, but doesn't seem that special**" (the middling wavers)
- "**Used it for a week, saves me 30 minutes a day**" (the higher works it diligently)

You stare at these three comments, uncomfortable — because the one being laughed at is the most visible, reposts the most.

**Laozi would say: being laughed at doesn't equal product failure**.

Your 1000 "higher" users — they **aren't praising you on social media**, they **are quietly using**. They won't post "I saved 30 minutes with X today" because this is too small to be worth posting.

The "laughter" you see — is the lower trying to measure "what they don't understand" with what they do understand, can't, so laugh.

**A product's real success isn't "no one laughed after launch", it's "someone quietly used it for a week"**.
chapters.action_cn: 这周,被嘲笑了**别急着回应**。先停 3 秒,问自己:"他是上中下哪一类?"如果是下士,记住:**他的笑是道本来会引起的反应**。
chapters.action_en: This week, if you're laughed at, **don't respond immediately**. Pause for 3 seconds, ask yourself: "Which of the three am I dealing with?" If it's the lower, remember: **his laugh is the response the Dao was always going to provoke**.

chapters.original_cn:
道生一,一生二,二生三,三生万物。
万物负阴而抱阳,冲气以为和。
人之所恶,唯孤、寡、不毂,而王公以为称。
故物,或损之而益,或益之而损。
人之所教,我亦教之。
强梁者不得其死,吾将以为教父。
chapters.original_en:
The Dao gives birth to the One.
The One gives birth to the Two.
The Two gives birth to the Three.
The Three gives birth to the ten thousand things.
The ten thousand things carry yin on their backs and embrace yang.
Clashing qi forms harmony.
What people dislike — orphan, widow, unable — yet kings and lords use these as their titles.
Therefore: things are sometimes diminished and thereby increased.
Sometimes increased and thereby diminished.
What people teach, I also teach.
The violent do not die a natural death.
I will take this as the father of all teaching.
chapters.tongshi_cn:
这一章,大部分人第一反应是"老子在讲创世"——"道生一,一生二,二生三,三生万物",听着像神话。

但这章真正要说的不是"道怎么生成宇宙",是**"道怎么生成万物,中间那一步是什么"**——答案是"和"。

---

先看"道生一,一生二,二生三,三生万物"——这不是"一个东西分裂成 N 个东西",是**"道怎么一层一层"显化"的层级"**。

- **道** = 整张图,所有可能
- **一** = 第一件具体的东西
- **二** = 一分裂成两(从"一个"变"对立的两面")
- **三** = 两边加上"中间的力量"——也就是下一句的"冲气"
- **万物** = 三层稳定之后,所有具体的东西

**关键不是"一二三"这个数,关键是"三"不是"二分裂出来的",是"二之间生的"**。

---

然后老子说了一句真正重要的话:

> **万物负阴而抱阳,冲气以为和。**

"负"= 背,"抱"= 怀。

意思是:**万物都背着一个"阴",抱着一个"阳"——中间用"冲气"和**。

"冲气"不是某个具体的气,是**两边对冲、相互激荡时产生的那股"和气"**。

**重要: "和"不是"阴 + 阳"**。"和"是**阴和阳对冲时,中间生出的一种新东西**。

你做产品: 工程师说"我们要做得完美"(阳的极端),产品经理说"先上线再说"(阴的极端)。两个人吵一下午——吵出来的第三种方案"用 80% 的完美先上线,留 20% 给下版本"——**这个"第三方案"就是"冲气"**。

"和"不是没有矛盾——**"和"是矛盾激荡之后的产物**。

**没有"阴"和"阳",就没有"和"。没有对立,就没有"和气"。**

---

接着老子用了"王公自称孤寡不毂"——这跟第 39 章呼应,王公**自称最低**("孤"="孤儿","寡"="寡妇","不毂"="不能养活自己")。

老子用这个提醒:**"低"和"高"不是真的对立,是同一组的两个面**。王公称自己"孤寡不毂",正是因为知道自己是"高",所以反过来提醒自己"低"的部分。

"和气"就藏在"高"和"低"的中间。

---

接下来是这一章最重的一句:

> **强梁者不得其死,吾将以为教父。**

"强梁"= 用强、用硬的、硬刚的人。"不得其死"= 死的时候没死好/走得不顺。

**"吾将以为教父"**——"教父"这里不是 godfather 的意思,是**"教学的起点/根本"**。老子说:**"用强的人终不得好结果,这是我所有教导的起点"**。

这是老子把"用强"和"不得好结果"绑死——但他**不诅咒任何人**。他只是在讲一个他观察到的规律: **用强的人,结局通常没走好**。

"教父"是"教之始"——**老子所有的"不强"的教导,都是从这一句起的**。
chapters.tongshi_en:
Most people's first reaction: "Laozi is talking about creation" — "the Dao gives birth to the One, the One to the Two, the Two to the Three, the Three to the ten thousand things" — sounds mythical.

But what this chapter really says is **not "how the Dao created the universe", but "how the Dao gives birth to the ten thousand things, what is the middle step"** — the answer is "harmony".

---

First, "the Dao gives birth to the One, the One to the Two..." — this is **not "one thing splitting into N things", it's the layer in which the Dao "manifests"** step by step.

- **Dao** = the whole picture, all possibilities
- **One** = the first concrete thing
- **Two** = one splits into two (from "one" to "two opposing sides")
- **Three** = the two plus "the force in the middle" — that is, the "clashing qi" in the next line
- **Ten thousand things** = once the three layers are stable, all concrete things

**The point is not the number "1-2-3", the point is "Three" doesn't come from "Two splitting", it comes from "between the Two"**.

---

Then Laozi says the actually important line:

> **The ten thousand things carry yin on their backs and embrace yang. Clashing qi forms harmony.**

"Carry" means "to bear on the back", "embrace" means "to hold in the arms".

Meaning: **the ten thousand things all carry a "yin" and embrace a "yang" — in the middle, "clashing qi" forms harmony**.

"Clashing qi" is not some specific qi — it's **the "harmonious qi" generated when the two sides clash and stimulate each other**.

**Important: "harmony" is not "yin + yang". "Harmony" is the new thing that arises when yin and yang clash**.

You build a product: the engineer says "we have to build it perfectly" (yang extreme), the product manager says "ship it first, talk later" (yin extreme). The two argue for an afternoon — out comes the third plan "ship 80% perfection, leave 20% for the next version" — **this "third plan" is the "clashing qi"**.

"Harmony" is not the absence of contradiction — **"harmony" is the product of contradiction** clashing.

**Without "yin" and "yang", there is no "harmony". Without opposition, there is no "harmonious qi"**.

---

Then Laozi uses "kings and lords call themselves orphan, widow, unable" — this echoes chapter 39, kings and lords **call themselves the lowest** ("orphan" = orphan, "widow" = widow, "unable" = cannot support themselves).

Laozi uses this to remind: **"low" and "high" are not truly opposed, they are two sides of the same set**. Kings and lords call themselves "orphan, widow, unable" precisely because they know they are "high", so they remind themselves of the "low" part.

"Harmonious qi" hides in the middle of "high" and "low".

---

The heaviest line in this chapter is next:

> **The violent do not die a natural death. I will take this as the father of all teaching.**

"Violent" = those who use force, hardness, brute force. "Do not die a natural death" = when they die, it doesn't go well / they don't die smoothly.

**"I will take this as the father of all teaching"** — "father of all teaching" here is not godfather; it means **"the starting point, the foundation of teaching"**. Laozi says: **"the violent do not die well, this is the starting point of all my teaching"**.

This is Laozi binding "using force" to "not dying well" — but he **curses no one**. He is just describing a pattern he observed: **those who use force, usually don't end well**.

"Father of teaching" is "the beginning of teaching" — **all of Laozi's "non-force" teaching starts with this line**.
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"道生一,一生二,二生三,三生万物"读成**"道创造了一切"**——这是错的。

老子**没说"道创造"**。老子说的是**"道生了'一'——'一'生了'二'——'二'生了'三'——'三'生了万物"**。

**"生"是"使它显化",不是"凭空创造"**。你做产品——"产品"不是被你"创造"出来的,是**被你"显化"出来的**——你让一个本来在脑子里的东西,变成真的。

更深一层——"道生一"的"一"是什么?

**是"你的第一个具体决定"**。

你做产品的第一天,你说"做 XX 类工具"——这就是你的"一"。然后你分裂出"用户是谁"+"怎么做"——这是"二"。然后你加上"技术栈"——这是"三"。然后才是"具体功能 / 具体页面 / 具体按钮"——这是"万物"。

**你的"产品"从你说出"做 XX"那一刻就开始生万物了。**

**"道"是什么?道是"你为什么做这个产品"那个最初的、最模糊的冲动。**
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "the Dao gives birth to the One, the One to the Two, the Two to the Three, the Three to the ten thousand things" as **"the Dao created everything"** — wrong.

Laozi **didn't say "the Dao created"**. Laozi said **"the Dao gave birth to 'One' — 'One' to 'Two' — 'Two' to 'Three' — 'Three' to the ten thousand things"**.

**"Give birth" is "make it manifest", not "create from nothing"**. You build a product — "the product" is not "created" by you, it is **"manifested" by you** — you take something that was in your head and make it real.

One level deeper — what is "One" that the Dao gives birth to?

**It is "your first concrete decision"**.

The first day you build a product, you say "build an XX type of tool" — this is your "One". Then you split into "who is the user" + "how to do it" — this is "Two". Then you add "tech stack" — this is "Three". Then comes "specific features / specific pages / specific buttons" — this is "ten thousand things".

**Your "product" started giving birth to ten thousand things the moment you said "build XX"**.

**What is "Dao"? Dao is "why you build this product" — that initial, most vague impulse**.
chapters.scene_cn:
你 1 年前开始做产品,创始团队 3 个人:CEO、CTO、你(PM)。

那时候你跟 CTO 吵需求实现方式,你俩都是"阳"——强硬,直接,3 个月出 2 个版本。

1 年后你招了 30 个人,你意识到: **你和 CTO 再也不能硬吵了**——因为你们俩吵架,30 个人都在看。

这时候你做了一件事: **加一个"和气"角色——HR/OC**。

HR 跟 CTO 谈"团队节奏",HR 跟你谈"产品节奏",HR 在中间,**把你们俩的"阴"和"阳"接住,不让它对冲得太厉害**。

你之前以为"和气"= 妥协、= 软、= 没人吵架。

**错了。"和气"是"让阴和阳继续对冲,但不让它爆"。**

**没有"和气"角色,你和 CTO 的"硬"会爆——爆的方式是 30 个人 2 个月走 5 个人,或者产品跑偏 3 个月。**

**有"和气"角色,你和 CTO 还是"硬"——但硬被消化成"中"——中生出新方案"v2 推后一个月,核心功能保留"。**

**这就是"三生万物"——阴 + 阳 + 和气 = 新的、稳定的"万物"**。
chapters.scene_en:
You started a product 1 year ago, founding team of 3: CEO, CTO, you (PM).

Back then you and the CTO argued about how to implement features, you two were both "yang" — hard, direct, 3 months shipped 2 versions.

1 year later, you hire 30 people, you realize: **you and the CTO can no longer argue hard** — because when you two argue, 30 people are watching.

Then you do one thing: **add a "harmony" role — HR/OC**.

HR talks to CTO about "team rhythm", HR talks to you about "product rhythm", HR is in the middle, **holding your "yin" and the CTO's "yang", not letting them clash too hard**.

You used to think "harmony" = compromise, = soft, = no one arguing.

**Wrong. "Harmony" is "let yin and yang keep clashing, but don't let it explode"**.

**Without the "harmony" role, the "hard" between you and the CTO explodes — the way it explodes is 5 people leaving in 2 months, or the product going off-track for 3 months**.

**With the "harmony" role, you and the CTO are still "hard" — but the hardness is digested into "middle" — out of the middle comes a new plan "v2 pushed back 1 month, core features retained"**.

**This is "Three gives birth to the ten thousand things" — yin + yang + harmonious qi = new, stable "ten thousand things"**.
chapters.action_cn: 这周,下一次你和同事起冲突——别急着定胜负,**让那个"和气"留 3 秒**。吵完,问一句:"我们俩之间,能生出'第三种方案'吗?"
chapters.action_en: This week, the next time you and a colleague clash — **don't rush to declare a winner, let the "harmonious qi" sit for 3 seconds**. After the argument, ask: "Between the two of us, can a 'third plan' be born?"

chapters.original_cn:
天下之至柔,驰骋天下之至坚。
无有,入无间。
吾是以知无为之有益。
不言之教,无为之益,天下希及之。
chapters.original_en:
The softest of all things
rides over the hardest of all things.
Non-being enters where there is no gap.
From this I know the benefit of non-action.
The teaching without words,
the benefit of non-action —
few in the world can reach these.
chapters.tongshi_cn:
这一章第一句话,大部分人读成"柔能克刚"——然后当鸡汤。

但这句话的精确说法是:**"天下最柔的东西,能跑赢/穿透天下最硬的东西"**——"驰骋"是"奔跑、穿越",不是"打败"。

"柔"和"硬"在老子这里不是**道德对立**(柔=好,硬=坏),是**物理现象**:

---

**水是最柔的——但水能穿石。**

**空气是最柔的——但空气能让金属生锈。**

**网络是最柔的——但网络能穿透任何组织。**

老子用"驰骋"——"奔跑"——意思是**"柔不是'克刚',是'跑赢刚'"**。刚的东西跑不过柔的东西,因为刚的东西**有形状、有边界**,被卡住;柔的东西**没有形状、没有边界**,所以**能进任何没间隙的东西**。

---

第二句:

> **无有,入无间。**

"无有"= "无"和"有"——也可以读成"无形的"(无)和"有形的"(有)这两类东西。

"无间"= "没有间隙"。

整句的精确说法:**"无形的、有形的,都能进入'没有间隙'的东西"**——

- **"无形的"**能进"无间":水(无形的状态)、网络、声音、思想、文化——这些没有形状的东西,能进入任何没有间隙的东西
- **"有形的"**也能进"无间":针、刀、光——这些有形状的极小的东西,能进入没有间隙的东西

**关键是: 任何东西,只要够"小"或够"无",都能进入"没有间隙"的东西**。

你做产品: **一个"轻"的更新版本,比一个"重"的更新版本更容易进入用户的大脑**。

---

然后老子话锋一转,说自己从这两句得到的领悟:

> **吾是以知无为之有益。**

"无为之益"= "无为"的好处。

**"无为"不是"啥都不做"——"无为"是"不通过硬动作去做"**。

你带团队: 写一份 3 页的产品哲学文档,让团队自己读、自己理解、自己执行——这是"无为"——你**没有通过命令去做**。这是"不言之教"。

"不言之教"= **不用语言/命令/会议来教**——通过文档、文化、榜样、氛围来教。

**老子说"天下希及之"——"这个世上很少有人做得到"**。

大部分 leader 用"言"来教: 反复说、开会强调、PIP、绩效面谈。**这些人从来没想过: 写一份好的文档,比开 5 次会有效**。
chapters.tongshi_en:
Most people read the first line as "the soft conquers the hard" — then treat it as chicken soup.

But the precise meaning is: **"the softest thing under heaven can run through / penetrate the hardest thing under heaven"** — "rides over" is "to gallop, to penetrate", not "to defeat".

"Soft" and "hard" in Laozi are not **moral opposites** (soft = good, hard = bad), they are **physical phenomena**:

---

**Water is the softest — but water wears through stone.**

**Air is the softest — but air makes metal rust.**

**The internet is the softest — but the internet can penetrate any organization.**

Laozi uses "rides over" — "to gallop" — meaning **"soft doesn't 'conquer hard', it 'outruns hard'"**. Hard things can't outrun soft things, because hard things **have shape, have boundaries**, get stuck; soft things **have no shape, no boundary**, so they **can enter anything that has no gap**.

---

Second line:

> **Non-being enters where there is no gap.**

"Non-being" = "wu" and "you" — can also be read as "formless" (wu) and "formed" (you), the two kinds of things.

"No gap" = "wu jian".

The precise meaning: **"the formless and the formed can both enter 'the thing that has no gap'"** —

- **"Formless"** can enter "no gap": water (in formless state), the internet, sound, thought, culture — these have-no-shape things can enter anything that has no gap
- **"Formed"** can also enter "no gap": needles, knives, light — these formed, very small things can enter things that have no gap

**The point is: anything, as long as it's "small" or "formless", can enter "the thing that has no gap"**.

You build a product: **a "light" update version is easier to enter the user's brain than a "heavy" update version**.

---

Then Laozi pivots, saying what he learned from these two lines:

> **From this I know the benefit of non-action.**

"The benefit of non-action" = the benefit of "wu wei".

**"Non-action" is not "do nothing" — "non-action" is "do not do it through hard action"**.

You lead a team: write a 3-page product philosophy doc, let the team read it themselves, understand it themselves, execute it themselves — this is "non-action" — you **didn't do it through commands**. This is "the teaching without words".

"The teaching without words" = **don't use language / commands / meetings to teach** — use docs, culture, examples, atmosphere to teach.

**Laozi says "few in the world can reach these" — "few people in this world can do this"**.

Most leaders use "words" to teach: keep saying, meeting-emphasize, PIP, performance review. **These people never thought: writing a good doc is more effective than holding 5 meetings**.
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"天下之至柔,驰骋天下之至坚"读成**"老子叫人软,不能硬"**——这是道德教化。

**错的。**

老子**没说"你要软"**——老子**描述了一个物理现象**: 柔的东西能跑赢硬的东西。

什么意思?

- 你做产品,做一个"硬"的功能(代码量大、逻辑严密的复杂功能)——它**有形状、有边界**,容易被卡住
- 你做产品,做一个"软"的功能(轻量、灵活、可配置)——它**没有固定形状**,容易进入任何用户场景

**"软"的产品,长期比"硬"的产品跑得远**——不是因为它"好",是因为它**没有边界,哪里都能进**。

更深的反常识:

> **"至柔"不是"妥协"——"至柔"是"没有形状,所以能进入所有形状"**。

你做产品、做团队、做人生——**你不是变"软",你是**放弃"固定的形状"——这样你才能进入任何场景**。

"硬"的人,只能做"硬"的事。"软"的人,任何事都能做。
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "the softest of all things rides over the hardest of all things" as **"Laozi tells you to be soft, can't be hard"** — this is moral teaching.

**Wrong.**

Laozi **didn't say "you must be soft"** — Laozi **described a physical phenomenon**: soft things can outrun hard things.

What does it mean?

- You build a product, build a "hard" feature (large codebase, tightly-logic complex feature) — it **has shape, has boundaries**, easy to get stuck
- You build a product, build a "soft" feature (lightweight, flexible, configurable) — it **has no fixed shape**, easy to enter any user scenario

**"Soft" products, in the long run, run farther than "hard" products — not because they are "good", but because they **have no boundary, can enter anywhere**.

A deeper counter-intuitive point:

> **"The softest" is not "compromise" — "the softest" is "no shape, so it can enter any shape"**.

You build a product, build a team, build a life — **you are not becoming "soft", you are** giving up "fixed shape" — so you can enter any scenario.

A "hard" person can only do "hard" things. A "soft" person can do anything.
chapters.scene_cn:
你做 PM 第 3 年,带 30 人团队。

你发现一个问题: 每个月你要在 1:1 上对每个下属说同样的话——"我们的产品要先把核心功能做扎实,不要老追新功能"——你说了 10 遍,下个月他们又忘了。

然后你做了一件事: **把这 10 遍的内容写进一份 3 页的"产品哲学"文档**——放在团队 wiki 第一页。

下个月,新来的实习生读了这个文档,主动提了 3 个"扎实做"的方向——**他自己读了,他没听过你说**。

你 1:1 那个老下属,某天突然说"我最近在想,我们是不是应该把 A 功能砍了,专心做 B"——**他没等你 1:1 提醒,他被文档影响了**。

**你之前说 10 遍,大家没记住;文档放上去,大家慢慢吸收——这叫"不言之教"**。

你之前以为"教"= "说"。

**错了。"教"也可以是"让对的语言/文字/文化自然存在"——然后别人自己来取。**

**这才是"无为之益"——你没催、没推、没说,但大家在 3 个月后自己走过来。**
chapters.scene_en:
You're a 3rd-year PM, leading a 30-person team.

You notice a problem: every month in 1:1s, you say the same thing to every subordinate — "our product has to nail the core features first, stop chasing new features" — you say it 10 times, next month they forget again.

Then you do one thing: **write that "10 times" content into a 3-page "product philosophy" doc — put it on the team wiki's first page**.

Next month, a new intern reads the doc, proactively proposes 3 "do-it-solid" directions — **he read it himself, he never heard you say it**.

That old subordinate from your 1:1, one day suddenly says "I've been thinking lately, should we cut feature A and focus on B" — **he didn't wait for your 1:1 reminder, he was influenced by the doc**.

**You said it 10 times before, people didn't remember; put the doc up, people slowly absorb — this is called "the teaching without words"**.

You used to think "teach" = "say".

**Wrong. "Teach" can also be "let the right language / text / culture naturally exist" — then others come to take it themselves**.

**This is "the benefit of non-action" — you didn't push, didn't chase, didn't say, but 3 months later people walked over themselves**.
chapters.action_cn: 这周,挑你**最近重复说过的 5 句话**——把它们写进一份**"产品/团队文化"文档**,放在团队 wiki 第一页。下个月,看看你 1:1 上要重复几次——如果 1:1 上一句都不用重复,**说明"不言之教"已经生效**。
chapters.action_en: This week, pick the **5 sentences you've repeated lately** — write them into a **"product / team culture" doc**, put it on the team wiki's first page. Next month, see how many times you have to repeat in 1:1 — if you don't have to repeat even once in 1:1, **"the teaching without words" is already in effect**.

chapters.original_cn:
名与身孰亲?
身与货孰多?
得与亡孰病?
是故甚爱必大费,
多藏必厚亡。
知足不辱,知止不殆,可以长久。
chapters.original_en:
Fame or self, which is dearer?
Self or wealth, which is more?
Gain or loss, which is the greater disease?
Therefore: excessive love must cost a great expenditure.
Excessive hoarding must suffer a great loss.
Know contentment and be without disgrace.
Know when to stop and be without danger.
Then you can endure long.
chapters.tongshi_cn:
这一章,大部分人读成"老子叫你不爱名声"。

但老子**没说"不爱名声"**——老子**问你三个问题**——

---

> **名与身孰亲?**
> **身与货孰多?**
> **得与亡孰病?**

三个反问,问的是同一件事:**你更在乎哪个?**

- **"名"**(名声/品牌/名誉)和"身"(你自己/你的身体/你这个人)——**哪个跟你更亲**?
- **"身"**和"货"(财富/物质/股票/房子)——**哪个对你更多**?
- **"得"**(得到)和"亡"(失去)——**哪个让你更焦虑/生病**?

老子**没给答案**——他用反问,让你自己回答。

但他**给了判断标准**——

> **是故甚爱必大费,多藏必厚亡。**

- "甚爱"= 太爱——**太爱的东西,你必须花大力气去维持**——这个"大费"就是"太爱"的代价
- "多藏"= 藏得多——**藏得多的东西,失去的厚度也越大**——你存 100 万,丢 100 万的痛,比存 1 万、丢 1 万的痛大 100 倍

**结构上,这两句不是诅咒,是数学**——

- 你越爱一个东西,你投入在它身上的精力越多
- 你投入越多,失去的时候越痛
- 失去越痛,你越焦虑,越不敢放下,越投入——**循环开始**

---

然后老子说真正重要的话:

> **知足不辱,知止不殆,可以长久。**

- "知足"= 知道什么状态是"够的"
- "知止"= 知道什么时候该停
- "不辱"= 不会被辱
- "不殆"= 不会疲/危
- "可以长久"= 你可以走得更远

**"知足"不是"少欲望"**——"知足"是**"知道'够'在哪里"**。

你不知道"够在哪里"——你永远没够,你一直追。

**"知止"不是"早停"**——"知止"是**"知道在什么点停最合适"**。

你不知道"在哪停"——你跑过头,你停不下来,你爆。
chapters.tongshi_en:
Most people read this chapter as "Laozi tells you not to love fame".

But Laozi **didn't say "don't love fame"** — Laozi **asks you three questions** —

---

> **Fame or self, which is dearer?**
> **Self or wealth, which is more?**
> **Gain or loss, which is the greater disease?**

Three rhetorical questions, asking the same thing: **which do you care about more?**

- **"Fame"** (reputation / brand / name) and "self" (you / your body / you the person) — **which is closer to you**?
- **"Self"** and "wealth" (money / material / stocks / house) — **which is more to you**?
- **"Gain"** (getting) and "loss" (losing) — **which makes you more anxious / sick**?

Laozi **didn't give an answer** — he uses rhetorical questions, lets you answer yourself.

But he **gave the criteria** —

> **Therefore: excessive love must cost a great expenditure. Excessive hoarding must suffer a great loss.**

- "Excessive love" = loving too much — **what you love too much, you must spend great effort to maintain** — this "great expenditure" is the cost of "loving too much"
- "Excessive hoarding" = hoarding too much — **what you hoard too much, the loss is also thicker** — you save 1 million, losing 1 million hurts 100 times more than saving 10k, losing 10k

**Structurally, these two lines are not curses, they are math** —

- The more you love something, the more energy you invest in it
- The more you invest, the more it hurts to lose
- The more it hurts to lose, the more anxious you are, the less you dare let go, the more you invest — **the loop begins**

---

Then Laozi says what really matters:

> **Know contentment and be without disgrace. Know when to stop and be without danger. Then you can endure long.**

- "Know contentment" = knowing what state is "enough"
- "Know when to stop" = knowing when to stop
- "Without disgrace" = won't be disgraced
- "Without danger" = won't be exhausted / endangered
- "Can endure long" = you can go farther

**"Know contentment" is not "less desire"** — "know contentment" is **"knowing where 'enough' is"**.

You don't know "where enough is" — you never have enough, you keep chasing.

**"Know when to stop" is not "stop early"** — "know when to stop" is **"knowing at which point to stop is most appropriate"**.

You don't know "where to stop" — you run past, you can't stop, you blow.
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"知足不辱,知止不殆,可以长久"读成**"佛系/躺平/少欲望"**——这是误读。

**老子没说"少欲望"**——老子说的是**"知道'够'在哪里"**。

什么意思?

- 你有 100w,你**知道 100w 是"够"**——你继续做你爱的工作——**不辱**(你不会因为股票跌而焦虑到辞职)
- 你不知道 100w 是"够"——你继续追 200w——**多藏**——200w 跌 50%,你**厚亡**

**"知足"是"知道在哪个点停"——不是"停在少的位置"**。

你做产品,做到 DAU 100w——你**知道 100w 是"够"**——你继续做对用户有用的事——你**可以长久**。

你不知道 100w 是"够"——你非要追 1000w——**你开始走捷径**——开始做"数字游戏"——**不殆**(你最终疲掉)。

**"知足"的人不是"躺的人"——"知足"的人是"知道在哪停,不停在少的位置,也不追到多的位置"的人。**
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "know contentment and be without disgrace, know when to stop and be without danger, then you can endure long" as **"Buddhist / lying flat / less desire"** — this is misreading.

**Laozi didn't say "less desire"** — Laozi said **"knowing where 'enough' is"**.

What does it mean?

- You have 1 million, you **know 1 million is "enough"** — you keep doing work you love — **without disgrace** (you won't be so anxious about stock drops that you quit)
- You don't know 1 million is "enough" — you keep chasing 2 million — **hoarding** — 2 million drops 50%, you **suffer great loss**

**"Know contentment" is "knowing at which point to stop" — not "stopping at less"**.

You build a product, get to 1M DAU — you **know 1M is "enough"** — you keep doing what is useful for users — you **can endure long**.

You don't know 1M is "enough" — you insist on chasing 10M — **you start taking shortcuts** — start playing "number games" — **not without danger** (you eventually burn out).

**A "content" person is not a "lying flat" person — a "content" person is "knowing where to stop, not stopping at less, not chasing to more"**.
chapters.scene_cn:
你做 PM 第 5 年,升 VP。公司给你 50w 股票。

你做了 5 年 PM,月入从来没这么高过。股票 vesting 4 年,意味着你要继续待 4 年。

你开始**每周一看股价**。

然后你发现:

- 股价涨,你**比谁都开心**——但你**没真花那钱**,因为 vesting 没到
- 股价跌,你**比谁都不开心**——你**开始想"我是不是该跳"**
- 你**原本爱工作**——现在你**爱钱**——你开始选项目时,**先看哪个项目股票加成多**,不看哪个项目对用户最有用

**你多藏了"50w 股票"——你多了"厚亡"的风险**——

- 跌 30%,你 15w 没了
- 你之前没股票,你**不焦虑**——现在你**每天焦虑**
- 你**没有更爱工作**——你**更爱股票**

**老子会说: 你"多藏必厚亡"——你本来可以"知足"——你本来"知止"——但你选了"更多"。**

**3 年后,你回头看——你 5 年 PM 时做的产品,可能比 VP 3 年做的产品更有意义。**
chapters.scene_en:
You're a 5th-year PM, just promoted to VP. The company gives you 500k in stock.

You've been a PM for 5 years, you've never earned this much. The stock vests over 4 years, meaning you need to stay 4 more years.

You start **checking the stock price every Monday**.

Then you realize:

- Stock goes up, you're **happier than anyone** — but you **haven't actually spent the money**, because it's not vested
- Stock goes down, you're **sadder than anyone** — you **start thinking "should I jump ship"**
- You **originally loved your work** — now you **love the money** — you start picking projects, **first looking at which project has the best stock bonus**, not which project is most useful to users

**You hoarded "500k in stock" — you took on the risk of "great loss"** —

- Drops 30%, you lose 150k
- Before the stock, you **weren't anxious** — now you're **anxious every day**
- You **don't love your work more** — you **love the stock more**

**Laozi would say: you "hoarded must suffer great loss" — you could have "known contentment" — you could have "known when to stop" — but you chose "more"**.

**3 years later, you look back — the product you made in 5 years as PM might be more meaningful than the 3 years as VP**.
chapters.action_cn: 这周,打开你的**银行/股票账户**——看那些数字——**问自己:"这些数字让我焦虑吗?"**——如果焦虑,问一句:"**我能不能回到不看的时候?**"——如果能,**回到不看**——这就是"知足"。
chapters.action_en: This week, open your **bank / stock account** — look at those numbers — **ask yourself: "do these numbers make me anxious?"** — if anxious, ask: "**can I go back to not looking?**" — if yes, **go back to not looking** — this is "knowing contentment".

chapters.original_cn:
大成若缺,其用不弊。
大盈若冲,其用不穷。
大直若屈,大巧若拙,大辩若讷。
躁胜寒,静胜热。
清静为天下正。
chapters.original_en:
The greatest accomplishment seems deficient,
yet its use is not exhausted.
The greatest fullness seems empty,
yet its use is not ended.
The greatest straightness seems bent.
The greatest skill seems clumsy.
The greatest eloquence seems stammering.
Movement overcomes cold.
Stillness overcomes heat.
Clarity and stillness are the standards of the world.
chapters.tongshi_cn:
这一章,大部分人第一反应是"大成若缺 = 大成看起来像缺"——然后是鸡汤语感,没感觉。

但这一章,老子其实在做一件事:**给"大成"列一个对照表**——把"大成"和"看起来像缺"绑在一起。

---

> **大成若缺,其用不弊。**

"大成"= 真正完成/完美的东西;"若缺"= 看起来"有缺";"不弊"= 不会坏。

"真正完美的东西,看起来像有缺——它能用很久不坏。"

**这是个反常的论断**: 完美的东西居然看起来"有缺"?

"缺"不是"坏"。老子用的"缺",是**"还有空间"**。

你做产品: 一个真正完美的产品,不是"加无可加",是**"还差一点点"——"还差一点点"是它能长期不坏的原因**。

一个"加无可加"的产品——它**没有留空间给未来**——它容易被时间淘汰。

一个"看起来还有缺"的产品——它**有留白**——它**有空间被升级**——它能一直用。

---

接着是 3 个并列的"反向"——

> **大盈若冲,其用不穷。**

"大盈"= 真正满的东西;"若冲"= 看起来"空";"不穷"= 不会用尽。

你做产品: 一个真正"满"的产品,不是"功能塞满",是**"看起来还有空位"**。

"看起来还有空位"的产品——你**想加功能,知道往哪加**——**它能用很久不穷**。

"塞满"的产品——你想加,不知道往哪加——**你必须删功能才能加新功能**——**它用一段就穷**。

---

> **大直若屈。**

"大直"= 真正直的;"若屈"= 看起来"弯"。

你做产品: 一个真正"直对用户"的产品,不是"事事直说",是**"该弯的时候弯"**——"该弯"= "知道在什么场景说软话"。

你做朋友: 一个真正"直"的朋友,不是"啥都直说",是**"知道什么时候该软"**。

---

> **大巧若拙。**

"大巧"= 真正巧的;"若拙"= 看起来"笨"。

你做产品: 一个真正"巧"的产品,不是"功能炫技",是**"用户用着简单"——用户感觉"没巧"**。

iPhone 看起来"啥都没巧"——但每个交互都"刚刚好"——**这才是"大巧"**。

---

> **大辩若讷。**

"大辩"= 真正能辩的;"若讷"= 看起来"嘴笨"。

你开会: 一个真正"能辩"的人,不是"抢话+输出快",是**"大部分时候闭嘴,关键时候一句话"**。

---

然后老子说"躁胜寒,静胜热"——

> **躁胜寒,静胜热。清静为天下正。**

"躁"= 动;"寒"= 冷——"动"能治"冷"。

"静"= 静;"热"= 热——"静"能治"热"。

**"清静"是"天下正"——"天下正"= "天下的标准/正确的状态"。**

"清静"不是"啥都不做"——"清静"是**"清楚+静"**——**"知道什么清楚,然后不乱动"**。

**"清"是知道"在什么范围里动"——"静"是"知道不在那个范围时不动"。**

**这才是"正"——"正"是"标准"——"清静"是"判断正不正的标准"。**
chapters.tongshi_en:
Most people's first reaction: "great accomplishment seems deficient" — then chicken-soup vibes, no feeling.

But in this chapter, Laozi is doing one thing: **making a comparison table for "great accomplishment"** — binding "great accomplishment" and "seeming lacking" together.

---

> **The greatest accomplishment seems deficient, yet its use is not exhausted.**

"Great accomplishment" = truly completed / perfect things; "seems deficient" = looks "lacking"; "not exhausted" = won't break.

"Truly perfect things look like they have a deficiency — they can be used a long time without breaking."

**This is a counter-intuitive claim**: perfect things actually look "deficient"?

"Lacking" is not "broken". The "deficient" Laozi uses is **"still has space"**.

You build a product: a truly perfect product is not "nothing more to add", it is **"still missing a little bit" — "still missing a little bit" is why it can last a long time without breaking**.

A "nothing more to add" product — it **has no room left for the future** — it easily gets replaced by time.

A "looks like it has a deficiency" product — it **has whitespace** — it **has room to be upgraded** — it can keep being used.

---

Then come 3 parallel "reversals" —

> **The greatest fullness seems empty, yet its use is not ended.**

"Greatest fullness" = truly full things; "seems empty" = looks "empty"; "not ended" = won't run out.

You build a product: a truly "full" product is not "packed with features", it is **"looks like it still has room"**.

A "looks like it still has room" product — you **want to add features, you know where to add** — **it can be used a long time without running out**.

A "packed" product — you want to add, don't know where — **you have to delete features to add new ones** — **it runs out in a while**.

---

> **The greatest straightness seems bent.**

"Greatest straightness" = truly straight; "seems bent" = looks "bent".

You build a product: a truly "straight to the user" product is not "say everything straight", it is **"bent when needed"** — "bent when needed" = "knowing which scenario to use soft language".

You make friends: a truly "straight" friend is not "say everything straight", it is **"knowing when to be soft"**.

---

> **The greatest skill seems clumsy.**

"Greatest skill" = truly skillful; "seems clumsy" = looks "clumsy".

You build a product: a truly "skillful" product is not "feature flexing", it is **"users find it simple" — users feel "no skill"**.

iPhone looks "no skill" — but every interaction is "just right" — **this is "great skill"**.

---

> **The greatest eloquence seems stammering.**

"Greatest eloquence" = truly eloquent; "seems stammering" = looks "tongue-tied".

You're in a meeting: a truly "eloquent" person is not "grab the floor + output fast", it is **"shut up most of the time, one sentence at the key moment"**.

---

Then Laozi says "movement overcomes cold, stillness overcomes heat" —

> **Movement overcomes cold. Stillness overcomes heat. Clarity and stillness are the standards of the world.**

"Movement" = activity; "cold" = cold — "movement" can cure "cold".

"Stillness" = still; "heat" = heat — "stillness" can cure "heat".

**"Clarity and stillness are the standards of the world" — "the standards of the world" = "the standard / correct state of the world"**.

"Clarity and stillness" is not "do nothing" — "clarity and stillness" is **"clear + still"** — **"knowing what is clear, then not moving rashly"**.

**"Clarity" is "knowing within which range to move" — "stillness" is "knowing not to move when outside that range"**.

**This is "the standard" — "the standard" is "the criterion for judgment" — "clarity and stillness" is "the criterion for judging what is standard"**.
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"大成若缺"读成**"假装谦虚"**——"我做得很好,但嘴上说'还有缺'"。

**错的。**

老子**没说"装"**——老子说"大成"本身"若缺"——**"大成"看起来"像缺",不是"大成"装"缺"**。

什么意思?

你做产品,你那个"完美"版本,不是"装"成"还有缺"——是**"完美"本身就有结构性的"缺"**——这个"缺"是"完美"的一部分。

**完美"是"有'缺'的完美"——不是"装'缺'的完美"。**

"假装谦虚"的"装"是表演——**老子已经在第 38 章拒绝"装"**——"上德不德,是以有德"——**真的"有缺"是有"留白"——不是装"缺"。**

**你做产品,做一个"看起来还有缺"的产品,不是"装作"还有缺——是"它真的还有缺——而这个'缺'是它能用 5 年的原因"。**
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "the greatest accomplishment seems deficient" as **"fake humility"** — "I did great, but say 'still deficient' on the surface".

**Wrong.**

Laozi **didn't say "pretend"** — Laozi said "great accomplishment" itself "seems deficient" — **"great accomplishment" looks "like it has a deficiency", it is not "great accomplishment" pretending "deficient"**.

What does it mean?

You build a product, your "perfect" version, is not "pretending" to "still have a deficiency" — it is **"perfection" itself has a structural "deficiency"** — this "deficiency" is part of "perfection".

**"Perfection" is "perfection with a deficiency" — not "perfection pretending deficiency"**.

"Faking humility" is performance — **Laozi already rejected "performance" in chapter 38** — "the highest virtue does not act virtuously, therefore it has virtue" — **the real "having a deficiency" is "having whitespace" — not "faking deficiency"**.

**You build a product, build a "looks like it still has a deficiency" product, not "pretending to still have a deficiency" — it really still has a deficiency — and this "deficiency" is why it can be used for 5 years**.
chapters.scene_cn:
你做 PM 第 4 年,做一个新功能,设计师/工程师/PM 三个角色都"完美主义"——

设计师说"色彩要再调 2 个版本"——你等。
工程师说"代码要再压一遍性能"——你等。
PM(你)说"功能要再加一个边缘 case"——你等。

3 个月后,你们终于达成"完美版本"——上线。

**用户反应: "挺好,但用着没感觉"**——因为用户感觉不到"完美"——他们感觉到的,是"完整"。

你看数据: 上线后 30 天,日活只涨了 5%——比之前那个"看起来还有缺"的版本涨得少。

那个"看起来还有缺"的版本,日活涨了 30%。

**为什么?**

因为用户感觉"它还有东西可以挖"——"它还有空间"——"我能用得越来越深"。

你那个"完美"版本,用户感觉"它就这样了"——**没有"留白"**——**用一段就换**。

**老子会说: "大成若缺"——你的"完美"上线版,缺的不是 bug,是"留白"**。
chapters.scene_en:
You're a 4th-year PM, building a new feature. The three roles — designer, engineer, PM — are all "perfectionists" —

Designer says "the colors need 2 more tweaks" — you wait.
Engineer says "the code needs another performance pass" — you wait.
PM (you) says "the feature needs one more edge case" — you wait.

3 months later, you finally reach the "perfect version" — ship it.

**User reaction: "It's fine, but using it doesn't feel right"** — because users don't feel "perfection" — what they feel is "complete".

You look at data: 30 days after launch, DAU only grew 5% — less than that "looks like it still has a deficiency" version.

That "looks like it still has a deficiency" version, DAU grew 30%.

**Why?**

Because users feel "it still has things to dig" — "it still has space" — "I can use it deeper and deeper".

Your "perfect" version, users feel "this is it" — **no "whitespace"** — **they switch after a while**.

**Laozi would say: "great accomplishment seems deficient" — your "perfect" shipping version, the deficiency is not a bug, the deficiency is "whitespace"**.
chapters.action_cn: 这周,选你**最自信的那个项目**——问一句:"**它缺什么?**"——如果你答不上来,**说明你太自信了**——你那个项目,可能正因为"没缺",才"用一段就换"。**找到那个"缺"——把它变成"留白"——这才是"大成"。**
chapters.action_en: This week, pick the **project you're most confident about** — ask: "**what is it missing?**" — if you can't answer, **that means you're too confident** — your project, precisely because "it doesn't have a deficiency", might be why "it's used for a while then switched". **Find that "deficiency" — turn it into "whitespace" — this is "great accomplishment"**.

chapters.original_cn:
天下有道,却走马以粪;
天下无道,戎马生于郊。
祸莫大于不知足,咎莫大于欲得。
故知足之足,常足矣。
chapters.original_en:
When the world has the Dao,
fast horses are led back to fertilize the fields.
When the world has no Dao,
war horses are bred in the suburbs.
No disaster is greater than not knowing "enough".
No fault is greater than wanting to gain.
Therefore: knowing the "enough" of knowing enough,
one is always enough.
chapters.tongshi_cn:
这一章,大部分人第一反应是"老子反战"——"有道"= 没有战争,"无道"= 有战争。

但老子这一章讲的不是"反战"——他讲的是**"有道时,马都被拉回去种地;无道时,战马在边郊(而不是战死在战场上)"**。

---

先看"天下有道,却走马以粪"——

"却"= 退;"走马"= 跑得快的战马;"粪"= 施肥、耕田。

**"有道时,战马都退回去耕田"**——不是"有道时没有马",是**"有道时,本来打仗用的马,被拉回去做民生的事"**。

意思是:**资源从"打仗"转向"民生"**。

---

再看"天下无道,戎马生于郊"——

"戎马"= 战马;"郊"= 城外、边郊;"生于"= 在(母马怀孕)生出。

**"无道时,战马在边郊出生"**——不是"无道时,战马被派出去"——是**"无道时,战马在(和平的)边郊出生"**。

等等——**"无道"不是更该打仗吗?为什么"战马"在"边郊"出生?**

老子的逻辑是:

**"无道"时,战马不再是"为了打仗而生"——是"为了能生而生"——资源被浪费在"无意义的扩张"上**。

**"有道"时,资源被收回(战马拉回去耕田)——**有道 = 资源被合理使用**。

**"无道"时,资源被无序扩张(战马在不需要打仗时还在生)——**无道 = 资源被挥霍**。

---

然后老子说真正重要的话:

> **祸莫大于不知足,咎莫大于欲得。**

- "祸莫大于"= 没有比这更大的祸
- "不知足"= 不知道"够"
- "咎莫大于"= 没有比这更大的错
- "欲得"= 想得到更多

**"不知足"是最大的祸——"想得到更多"是最大的错。**

"不知足"和"欲得"听起来很像——但老子分开讲——

- "不知足"= **不知道"够"在哪里**——你一直追,从来没停过
- "欲得"= **想得到更多**——你追到"够"了,还想要更多

**"不知足"是你没找到"够"——"欲得"是你找到"够"但不要"够"**。

---

最后一句:

> **故知足之足,常足矣。**

"知足之足"= 知道"够"的那个"够"——"知道'足'的'足'"。

**"知道'足'的本质"——你才"常足"——"常足"是"永远够"。**

第一层的"足"是状态——"我够"。
第二层的"足"是认知——"我知道'够'是什么"。

**"知道'够是什么'"比"我够"重要**——

你不知道"够是什么"——你**有 100w 还是不够**——你**没常足**。
你知道"够是什么"——你**有 10w 就够**——你**常足**。
chapters.tongshi_en:
Most people's first reaction: "Laozi is anti-war" — "has the Dao" = no war, "no Dao" = has war.

But this chapter is not "anti-war" — it says: **"when the Dao is present, horses are led back to farm; when the Dao is absent, war horses are bred in the suburbs (not dispatched to die in battle)"**.

---

First, "when the world has the Dao, fast horses are led back to fertilize the fields" —

"Lead back" = retreat; "fast horses" = the war horses that ran; "fertilize" = fertilize, farm.

**"When the Dao is present, war horses are led back to farm"** — not "when the Dao is present there are no horses", it is **"when the Dao is present, horses that were used for war are pulled back to do people's livelihood work"**.

Meaning: **resources shift from "war" to "people's livelihood"**.

---

Then "when the world has no Dao, war horses are bred in the suburbs" —

"War horses" = war horses; "suburbs" = outside the city, suburbs; "bred" = born (mares getting pregnant) and born.

**"When the Dao is absent, war horses are bred in the suburbs"** — not "when the Dao is absent, war horses are dispatched" — it is **"when the Dao is absent, war horses are born in (peaceful) suburbs"**.

Wait — **"no Dao" should mean more war, right? Why are "war horses" born in "suburbs"?**

Laozi's logic:

**"No Dao" = war horses are no longer "born to fight" — they are "born to be born" — resources are wasted on "meaningless expansion"**.

**"Has the Dao" = resources are recalled (war horses pulled back to farm) — has the Dao = resources are used reasonably**.

**"No Dao" = resources are chaotically expanded (war horses still being born when no war is needed) — no Dao = resources are squandered**.

---

Then Laozi says what really matters:

> **No disaster is greater than not knowing "enough". No fault is greater than wanting to gain.**

- "No disaster is greater than" = nothing is a greater disaster
- "Not knowing enough" = not knowing where "enough" is
- "No fault is greater than" = nothing is a greater fault
- "Wanting to gain" = wanting to get more

**"Not knowing enough" is the greatest disaster — "wanting to gain" is the greatest fault**.

"Not knowing enough" and "wanting to gain" sound similar — but Laozi separates them —

- "Not knowing enough" = **not knowing where "enough" is** — you keep chasing, never stop
- "Wanting to gain" = **wanting to get more** — you chased to "enough", but still want more

**"Not knowing enough" is you didn't find "enough" — "wanting to gain" is you found "enough" but don't want "enough"**.

---

The last line:

> **Therefore: knowing the "enough" of knowing enough, one is always enough.**

"Knowing the enough of knowing enough" = knowing the "enough" of "enough" — "knowing the 'enough' of 'enough'".

**"Knowing the essence of 'enough'" — you are "always enough" — "always enough" is "forever enough"**.

The first layer of "enough" is state — "I have enough".
The second layer of "enough" is cognition — "I know what 'enough' is".

**"Knowing 'what is enough'" is more important than "I have enough"** —

You don't know "what is enough" — you **have 1 million but still not enough** — you **are not always enough**.
You know "what is enough" — you **have 100k and it's enough** — you **are always enough**.
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"知足"读成**"你要少欲望/你要小富即安"**——这是误读。

**老子没说"小富即安"**——老子说的是**"知道'够'在哪里"**。

"有道"的公司,**不是"小"的公司**——是**"知道自己的'够'在哪里"的公司**。

- 你的"够"是"主业 1 个,DAU 1000w"——你**专心做主业**——**有道**
- 你的"够"是"主业 1 个 + 2 个新业务"——你**做 3 个**——**无道(扩张到不知道'够'了)**

**"知足"不是"少"——"知足"是"知道你的'够'在哪个具体的位置"。**

你做产品: **DAU 100w 是你的"够"**——你做 100w 的事——**有道**。

你不知道 100w 是你的"够"——你做 500w 的事——**无道**。

**500w 不一定比 100w 好——500w 是"扩张到不知道'够'了"——这种公司,18 个月后 80% 都倒了。**
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "knowing enough" as **"you should have less desire / you should be content with small riches"** — this is misreading.

**Laozi didn't say "content with small riches"** — Laozi said **"knowing where 'enough' is"**.

A "has the Dao" company, **is not a "small" company** — it is **a "knows where its 'enough' is" company**.

- Your "enough" is "1 main business, 10M DAU" — you **focus on the main business** — **has the Dao**
- Your "enough" is "1 main + 2 new" — you **do 3** — **no Dao (expanded past not knowing 'enough')**

**"Knowing enough" is not "less" — "knowing enough" is "knowing where your 'enough' is at the specific location"**.

You build a product: **DAU 1 million is your "enough"** — you do the 1M thing — **has the Dao**.

You don't know 1M is your "enough" — you do the 5M thing — **no Dao**.

**5M is not necessarily better than 1M — 5M is "expanded past not knowing 'enough'" — this kind of company, 80% collapse after 18 months**.
chapters.scene_cn:
你做 PM 第 5 年,公司刚融了 B 轮 5000w。

CEO 兴奋得不行——开 3 个新业务线——招 100 人——"必须扩张,这个窗口就 1 年"。

**这是"天下有道,却走马以粪"的反面**——

**不是"有道"时把战马拉回去种田——是"有道"时开更多战马去打仗。**

CEO 的逻辑:"有 5000w 不用,过期作废。"

**但老子会说: "祸莫大于不知足"——你**有 5000w 还想要 1 亿**——你"不知足"——这是"祸"。**

你 18 个月后看——3 个新业务线 2 个死了,招的 100 人走了 40——**资源被无序扩张消耗**。

---

反过来看另一家公司:

融资差——只有 1000w——CEO 决定"主业做扎实,不开新业务"。

**这是"有道"——资源被合理使用**——

**18 个月后,主业 DAU 翻 2 倍——**有道 = 资源被合理使用**。**
chapters.scene_en:
You're a 5th-year PM, your company just raised a B round of 50 million.

The CEO is ecstatic — open 3 new business lines — hire 100 people — "must expand, this window is only 1 year".

**This is the opposite of "when the world has the Dao, fast horses are led back to fertilize"** —

**Not "has the Dao" = war horses pulled back to farm — it is "has the Dao" = open more war horses to fight**.

The CEO's logic: "If we don't use the 50 million, it expires."

**But Laozi would say: "no disaster is greater than not knowing enough" — you **have 50 million but still want 100 million** — you "don't know enough" — this is "disaster"**.

18 months later you see — of the 3 new business lines, 2 die, of the 100 hired, 40 leave — **resources are chaotically expanded and consumed**.

---

On the other hand, another company:

Under-funded — only 10 million — CEO decides "main business solid, no new lines".

**This is "has the Dao" — resources are reasonably used** —

**18 months later, main business DAU doubled — has the Dao = resources are reasonably used**.
chapters.tension_cn:
**第 45 章**: "大成若缺, 其用不弊; 大盈若冲, 其用不穷"——大成——若缺——大盈——若冲。

**第 46 章**: "天下有道, 却走马以粪; 天下无道, 戎马生于郊"——有道——无道——"知足之足, 常足矣"。

两章是**"大成若缺+大盈若冲"+"有道+无道+知足之足=常足"**——

> **第 45 章: 大成若缺+大盈若冲(大成=若缺;大盈=若冲)**
> **第 46 章: 有道+无道+知足之足=常足(有道=走马以粪;无道=戎马生于郊)**

- 第 45 章教你"大成=若缺+大盈=若冲"
- 第 46 章教你"有道+无道+知足之足=常足"

**"大成若缺+大盈若冲"+"有道+无道+知足之足=常足"= 大成若缺+知足之足= 你在"道"。**
chapters.tension_en:
**Chapter 45**: "Great completion seems lacking, its use is not worn out; great fullness seems empty, its use is not exhausted" — great completion — seems lacking — great fullness — seems empty.

**Chapter 46**: "When the world has Dao, swift horses return to fertilize the fields; when the world lacks Dao, war horses breed on the borders" — has Dao — lacks Dao — "knowing the 'enough' of enough, ever enough".

Two chapters are **"great completion seems lacking + great fullness seems empty" + "has Dao + lacks Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough"** —

> **Chapter 45: great completion seems lacking + great fullness seems empty (great completion = seems lacking; great fullness = seems empty)**
> **Chapter 46: has Dao + lacks Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough (has Dao = horses fertilize; lacks Dao = horses breed)**

- Chapter 45 teaches you "great completion = seems lacking + great fullness = seems empty"
- Chapter 46 teaches you "has Dao + lacks Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough"

**"Great completion seems lacking + great fullness seems empty" + "has Dao + lacks Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough" = great completion seems lacking + knowing the 'enough' of enough = you are in "Dao".**
chapters.action_cn: 这周,看你公司最近 3 个月的开支——问一句:**"这些开支里,多少是因为不知道'够'而加的?"**——如果超过 30%,**停一半**——**这就是"知足"**。
chapters.action_en: This week, look at your company's expenses in the last 3 months — ask: **"of these expenses, how much was added because of not knowing 'enough'?"** — if more than 30%, **stop half** — **this is "knowing enough"**.

chapters.original_cn:
不出户,知天下;
不窥牖,见天道。
其出弥远,其知弥少。
是以圣人不行而知,不见而名,不为而成。
chapters.original_en:
Without going out the door,
one can know the world.
Without looking through the window,
one can see the Dao of heaven.
The further one goes,
the less one knows.
Therefore the sage knows without traveling,
sees without looking,
accomplishes without acting.
chapters.tongshi_cn:
这一章,大部分人第一反应是"老子叫人别出门,在屋里就能知道天下"——听起来像自大。

但老子**没说"别出门"**——老子**说"不出户(出门)也能知——但你'出'得越远,知道得越少"**。

---

先看"不出户,知天下;不窥牖,见天道"——

"户"= 门;"牖"= 窗;"窥"= 从孔里看;"天道"= 天的规律/结构。

**精确说法: "不出门就能知道天下;不看窗外就能见到天道"。**

但**不是说"不要出门/不要看窗外"**——是说**"有另一种'知'的方式,不需要通过'出门/看窗外'这种"**。

---

这种"另一种'知'"是什么?——看下一句:

> **其出弥远,其知弥少。**

"其"= 他(那些去远行的人);"弥"= 越。

**"你(那些去远行的人)走得越远,你'那种知'就越少"——注意: 老子没说"你知道的越少",他说的是"你'那种知'(通过远行得到的)越来越少"。**

什么意思?

你做用户调研——你**做 50 场用户访谈,看了 200 个工单**——你**收集的数据越来越多**——但你**"看得到结构"的能力越来越弱**——因为**数据淹没了结构**。

**老子不是说"别做调研"——老子说"调研做多了,反而离'结构'远"**。

你走 1 公里,你**能看清眼前 100 米**。
你走 100 公里,你**能看清眼前 100 米**——你**"看远"的能力没增,你"看近"的精度没变,但你"看结构"的能力降低了**。

---

然后老子说"圣人"——

> **是以圣人不行而知,不见而名,不为而成。**

"不行"= 不通过"行"(走);"知"= 知道。
"不见"= 不通过"见"(看);"名"= 命名(看清楚)。
"不为"= 不通过"为"(做);"成"= 成就。

**"圣人'不通过行来知','不通过看来名','不通过做来成'"**。

"行"是**"通过身体移动得到的'知'"**——比如出差、调研、采访。
"见"是**"通过眼睛看得到的'名'"**——比如看数据、看 PPT、看市场报告。
"为"是**"通过手动做得到的'成'"**——比如加班、赶进度、堆功能。

"圣人"——不靠这三种**——靠"结构"——靠"看着不动就能知道"。
chapters.tongshi_en:
Most people's first reaction: "Laozi tells you not to go out, in the house you can know the world" — sounds arrogant.

But Laozi **didn't say "don't go out"** — Laozi **said "you can know without going out — but the further you 'go', the less you 'know'"**.

---

First, "without going out the door, one can know the world; without looking through the window, one can see the Dao of heaven" —

"Door" = door; "window" = window; "looking through" = look through a hole; "Dao of heaven" = the pattern/structure of heaven.

**Precise meaning: "you can know the world without going out the door; you can see the Dao of heaven without looking through the window"**.

But **it does not mean "don't go out / don't look through the window"** — it means **"there is another way of 'knowing' that doesn't need to 'go out / look through the window' to"**.

---

What is this "another 'knowing'"? — see the next line:

> **The further one goes, the less one knows.**

"He" = him (those who go far); "the more" = the more.

**"You (those who go far) go further, your 'that kind of knowing' (obtained through traveling) gets less" — note: Laozi didn't say "you know less", he said "the 'knowing' you get through going far, gets less"**.

What does it mean?

You do user research — you **do 50 user interviews, look at 200 tickets** — you **collect more and more data** — but your **ability to "see the structure" gets weaker** — because **data drowns the structure**.

**Laozi is not saying "don't do research" — Laozi is saying "the more research you do, the further you are from 'structure'"**.

You walk 1 km, you **can see clearly the 100 meters in front of you**.
You walk 100 km, you **can see clearly the 100 meters in front of you** — your **"see far" ability didn't grow, your "see near" precision didn't change, but your "see structure" ability decreased**.

---

Then Laozi says "the sage" —

> **Therefore the sage knows without traveling, sees without looking, accomplishes without acting.**

"Without traveling" = not through "traveling" (walking); "knows" = knows.
"Without looking" = not through "looking" (seeing); "names" = name (see clearly).
"Without acting" = not through "acting" (doing); "accomplishes" = accomplishes.

**"The sage 'knows not through traveling', 'names not through looking', 'accomplishes not through acting'"**.

"Traveling" is **"knowing obtained through the body's movement"** — like business trips, research, interviews.
"Looking" is **"naming obtained through the eyes"** — like looking at data, looking at PPTs, looking at market reports.
"Acting" is **"accomplishing obtained through hand-doing"** — like working overtime, rushing progress, piling on features.

The "sage" — doesn't rely on these three — relies on "structure" — relies on "looking without moving to know".
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"不出户,知天下"读成**"你别出门/你别调研,坐在屋里就能知道"**——这是误读。

**老子没说"不调研"**——老子说**"有一种'知',不通过'出门'得到——这种'知'比'通过出门得到的'更接近'结构'"**。

什么意思?

你做产品决策:

- 你**走 50 个用户**——你**得到 50 个"个体偏好"**——你**没有"结构"**
- 你**走 5 个用户,但每个都问"为什么"**——你**得到 5 个"决策逻辑"**——你**有"结构"**

**"结构"是"5 个用户的决策逻辑"——不是"50 个用户的偏好"**。

你做战略:

- 你**做 100 场市场调研**——你**得到 100 个"市场声音"**——你**没有"市场结构"**
- 你**做 5 场深度访谈,每次都问"市场为什么是这样"**——你**得到 5 个"市场逻辑"**——你**有"市场结构"**

**"结构"是"少而深"——不是"多而广"**。

**"不出户"不是"闭门"——"不出户"是"用脑子里的结构看天下"——而不是"用脚跑遍天下"**。
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "without going out the door, one can know the world" as **"don't go out / don't do research, sit in the house and you can know"** — this is misreading.

**Laozi didn't say "don't research"** — Laozi said **"there is a 'knowing' that doesn't come through 'going out' — this 'knowing' is closer to 'structure' than 'knowing through going out'"**.

What does it mean?

You make product decisions:

- You **go through 50 users** — you **get 50 "individual preferences"** — you **have no "structure"**
- You **go through 5 users, but each time ask 'why'"** — you **get 5 "decision logics"** — you **have "structure"**

**"Structure" is "decision logics of 5 users" — not "preferences of 50 users"**.

You do strategy:

- You **do 100 market surveys** — you **get 100 "market voices"** — you **have no "market structure"**
- You **do 5 deep interviews, each time ask 'why is the market like this'"** — you **get 5 "market logics"** — you **have "market structure"**

**"Structure" is "few but deep" — not "many but broad"**.

**"Without going out" is not "behind closed doors" — "without going out" is "use the structure in your head to see the world" — not "use your feet to run all over the world"**.
chapters.scene_cn:
你做 PM 第 3 年,新人小李也做 PM。

你们都在做同一个功能。

你:**做了 50 场用户访谈,看了 200 个工单,做了 30 份调研报告**。
小李:**做了 5 场用户访谈,但他每次都问同一个核心问题**。

你们俩都做了"用户调研"——但你**信息量是小李的 10 倍**。

---

**会议上,产品方向之争**——

- 你:"我做了 50 场,数据显示用户喜欢 A。"
- 小李:"我也做了 5 场。但 5 场里**每个用户**都说: '我不要 A,我要 B。'"

**小李"知"到了"结构"——他要的是"做不做 A"的明确答案。**
**你"知"到了"数据"——但你"看不到"那个答案。**

---

**3 个月后**——

- A 方向上线,数据平平。
- B 方向上线(因为小李坚持),DAU 涨 30%。

**老子会说: "其出弥远,其知弥少"——你"出"得远(50 场),你"那种知"(通过访谈得到的)就少——小李"出"得近(5 场),他"那种知"就多(因为每次他都看到了"结构")。**
chapters.scene_en:
You're a 3rd-year PM, new PM Xiaoli is also a PM.

You're both working on the same feature.

You: **did 50 user interviews, looked at 200 tickets, made 30 research reports**.
Xiaoli: **did 5 user interviews, but each time he asked the same core question**.

You both did "user research" — but your **information volume is 10 times Xiaoli's**.

---

**In the meeting, the product direction debate** —

- You: "I did 50, the data shows users like A."
- Xiaoli: "I also did 5. But **every user** in those 5 said: 'I don't want A, I want B.'"

**Xiaoli "knew" the "structure" — what he wanted was the clear answer to "do A or not".**
**You "knew" the "data" — but you "couldn't see" that answer**.

---

**3 months later** —

- A direction shipped, data mediocre.
- B direction shipped (because Xiaoli insisted), DAU up 30%.

**Laozi would say: "the further one goes, the less one knows" — you "went" far (50), your "that kind of knowing" (through interviews) is less — Xiaoli "went" near (5), his "that kind of knowing" is more (because each time he saw the "structure")**.
chapters.tension_cn:
**第 46 章**: "天下有道, 却走马以粪; 天下无道, 戎马生于郊"——有道——无道——"知足之足, 常足矣"。

**第 47 章**: "不出户, 知天下; 不窥牖, 见天道"——不出户——知天下——不窥牖——见天道——"其出弥远, 其知弥少"。

两章是**"有道+无道+知足之足=常足"+"不出户+不窥牖+其出弥远其知弥少"**——

> **第 46 章: 有道+无道+知足之足=常足(有道=走马以粪;无道=戎马生于郊)**
> **第 47 章: 不出户+不窥牖+其出弥远其知弥少(不出户=知天下;其出=弥远其知=弥少)**

- 第 46 章教你"有道+无道+知足之足=常足"
- 第 47 章教你"不出户+不窥牖+其出弥远其知弥少"

**"有道+知足之足=常足"+"不出户+其出弥远其知弥少"= 知足+少出= 你在"道"。**
chapters.tension_en:
**Chapter 46**: "When the world has Dao, swift horses return to fertilize the fields; when the world lacks Dao, war horses breed on the borders" — has Dao — lacks Dao — "knowing the 'enough' of enough, ever enough".

**Chapter 47**: "Without going out the door, know the world; without peeking through the window, see the way of heaven" — without going out — know the world — without peeking — see the way of heaven — "the further you go, the less you know".

Two chapters are **"has Dao + lacks Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough" + "without going out + without peeking + the further you go the less you know"** —

> **Chapter 46: has Dao + lacks Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough (has Dao = horses fertilize; lacks Dao = horses breed)**
> **Chapter 47: without going out + without peeking + the further you go the less you know (without going out = know the world; the further you go = the less you know)**

- Chapter 46 teaches you "has Dao + lacks Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough"
- Chapter 47 teaches you "without going out + without peeking + the further you go the less you know"

**"Has Dao + knowing the 'enough' of enough = ever enough" + "without going out + the further you go the less you know" = knowing enough + less going out = you are in "Dao".**
chapters.action_cn: 这周,你做下一个产品决策前——问自己:**"我是要再收集 1 个数据点,还是退后一步看已有 100 个的结构?"**——如果答案是"退后一步",**退后一步**——**这才是"不出户知"**。

chapters.tongshi_cn:
这一章,大部分人第一反应是"老子反学习"——"为道日损"听起来像"学习没用,反而要减"。

但老子**没说"反学习"**——他**区分了两种事**:

---

> **为学日益,为道日损。**

"为学"= 追求学问;"日益"= 每天增加。
"为道"= 修习道;"日损"= 每天减少。

**精确说法: "追求学问,每天都在增加;修习道,每天都在减少"**。

**"为学"是"往里装东西"**——你读 1 本书,装 1 本;读 100 本,装 100 本。
**"为道"是"往里卸东西"**——你卸 1 个"装",卸 1 个;卸 100 个,卸 100 个。

**两者方向相反,不是同一个事**:

- **"为学"是"增加知识"**——这是好的——但它**会让你"知道得多,做得慢"**
- **"为道"是"减少预设"**——这是好的——它**会让你"知道得少,做得快"**

---

接着是关键的一句:

> **损之又损,以至于无为。**

"损"= 减少;"无为"= 不通过"做"的方式。

**"减少又减少,直到'不通过做的方式'"**。

"为道"不是"减到 0"——是"减到你不再'主动地做'"——减到**"你做的事,不通过'做'这个动作"**。

---

> **无为而无不为。**

"无为"= 不通过"做";"无不为"= 没有做不成的。

**"不通过'做'的方式,但一切事都做成"**。

这看起来矛盾——但意思是:

**"无为"不是"啥都不做"——是"不通过'硬做'的方式"——"无不为"是"不靠硬做,什么都能成"**。

---

然后老子把"取天下"和这个挂钩:

> **取天下常以无事,及其有事,又不足以取天下。**

"取天下"= 取得天下(治理天下/得到天下);"无事"= 不通过做事;"有事"= 通过做事。

**"取天下,通常靠'不通过做事';一旦你'通过做事',你就'取不了天下'"**。

"无事"不是"闲着"——"无事"是**"不通过'做'这个动作"**。
chapters.tongshi_en:
Most people's first reaction: "Laozi is anti-learning" — "the pursuit of the Dao decreases daily" sounds like "learning is useless, you should subtract".

But Laozi **didn't say "anti-learning"** — he **distinguished two different things**:

---

> **The pursuit of learning increases daily. The pursuit of the Dao decreases daily.**

"Pursuit of learning" = pursuing knowledge; "increases daily" = increases every day.
"Pursuit of the Dao" = practicing the Dao; "decreases daily" = decreases every day.

**Precise meaning: "pursuing knowledge, you increase every day; practicing the Dao, you decrease every day"**.

**"Pursuit of learning" is "loading things in"** — you read 1 book, load 1; read 100, load 100.
**"Pursuit of the Dao" is "unloading things out"** — you unload 1 "load", unload 1; unload 100, unload 100.

**They are in opposite directions, they are not the same thing**:

- **"Pursuit of learning" is "increasing knowledge"** — this is good — but it **will make you "know more, do slower"**
- **"Pursuit of the Dao" is "decreasing presupposition"** — this is good — it **will make you "know less, do faster"**

---

Next is the key line:

> **Decrease and again decrease, until you arrive at non-action.**

"Decrease" = reduce; "non-action" = not through "doing".

**"Decrease and again decrease, until 'not through the way of doing'"**.

"Pursuit of the Dao" is not "decrease to 0" — it is "decrease until you no longer 'actively do'" — decrease until **"what you do, doesn't go through the 'doing' action"**.

---

> **Through non-action, nothing is left undone.**

"Non-action" = not through "doing"; "nothing left undone" = nothing is not accomplished.

**"Not through the way of 'doing', but everything is accomplished"**.

This sounds contradictory — but it means:

**"Non-action" is not "do nothing" — it is "not through the way of 'hard doing'" — "nothing is left undone" is "without hard doing, everything can be accomplished"**.

---

Then Laozi ties "taking hold of the world" to this:

> **To take hold of the world, always rely on non-interference. Once you interfere, you are not fit to take hold of the world.**

"Take hold of the world" = take the world (govern the world / get the world); "non-interference" = not through doing; "interference" = through doing.

**"To take hold of the world, usually rely on 'not through doing'; once you 'go through doing', you 'cannot take hold of the world'"**.

"Non-interference" is not "idle" — "non-interference" is **"not through the 'doing' action"**.
chapters.counter_cn:
大部分人把"为学日益"读成**"学习越多越好"**——这是"为学"的方向——但**这只是老子描述的一半**。

老子**没说"为学不好"**——老子**说"为学"和"为道"是两种事**——

- "为学"是**"装"**——你装 100 本书,你"日益"
- "为道"是**"卸"**——你卸 100 个"装",你"日损"

**"为学"是加,"为道"是减——"为道"是"为学"之后的事——你装满了,再卸**。

什么意思?

你做产品: 

- 你**先"为学"**——读 5 本书,学 5 个方法——你**装**
- 你**再"为道"**——把 5 个方法,用到极致,直到你**不再"用方法"**——你**卸**
- 你**到"无为"**——你**不再调方法,你直接做——但你的"做"是基于 5 个方法已经内化的**——**"无为而无不为"**

**"为道"不是"不学"——"为道"是"学完,卸掉"**。

你 5 年读 100 本——**你一直在"为学"——你从不为道**——你装得越来越多,卸得越来越少——你"为学"装的东西,**反过来拖住你**。

**真正的高手 = "为学" + "为道"**——"为学"让他**有东西**——"为道"让他**卸得动**。
chapters.counter_en:
Most people read "the pursuit of learning increases daily" as **"the more you learn, the better"** — this is the direction of "pursuit of learning" — but **this is only half of what Laozi described**.

Laozi **didn't say "pursuit of learning is bad"** — Laozi **said "pursuit of learning" and "pursuit of the Dao" are two different things** —

- "Pursuit of learning" is **"loading"** — you load 100 books, you "increase daily"
- "Pursuit of the Dao" is **"unloading"** — you unload 100 "loads", you "decrease daily"

**"Pursuit of learning" is addition, "pursuit of the Dao" is subtraction — "pursuit of the Dao" comes after "pursuit of learning" — you load full, then unload**.

What does it mean?

You build a product:

- You **first "pursue learning"** — read 5 books, learn 5 methods — you **load**
- You **then "pursue the Dao"** — use the 5 methods to the extreme, until you **no longer "use methods"** — you **unload**
- You **arrive at "non-action"** — you **no longer mobilize methods, you directly do — but your "doing" is based on 5 methods already internalized** — **"through non-action nothing is left undone"**

**"Pursuit of the Dao" is not "don't learn" — "pursuit of the Dao" is "learn, then unload"**.

You 5 years read 100 books — **you keep "pursuing learning" — you never pursue the Dao** — you load more and more, unload less and less — the things you "pursue learning" loaded, **in turn hold you back**.

**A real master = "pursuit of learning" + "pursuit of the Dao"** — "pursuit of learning" lets him **have things** — "pursuit of the Dao" lets him **unload**.
chapters.scene_cn:
你做 PM 第 5 年,读了 100 本产品书,堆了 200 个方法论在脑子里。

你做决策时:**调 200 个方法论来对照**——慢——3 天才能给一个方案。

新人小李只读了 5 本产品书,但每本**用了 100 次**。

小李做决策时:**调 5 个核心方法**——快——半天给一个方案——**做的方案上 2 个月就涨 30%。**

你做决策时:**调 200 个方法**——3 天给一个方案——**上 2 个月涨 5%**。

---

**3 年后**:

- 你: **书越来越多,方法论越来越新,做出来的东西越来越复杂**——**升不上去**。
- 小李: **书就那 5 本,方法就那 5 个,做出来的东西越来越"对"**——**升到 VP**。

**老子会说: "为学日益"——你"为学",你"日益"——但你"为道"是"日损"——小李"为道",他"日损"——他把"为学"装的东西**损**了——损到"无为"——他"无为而无不为"**。
chapters.scene_en:
You're a 5th-year PM, read 100 product books, piled 200 methodologies in your head.

You make decisions: **mobilize 200 methodologies to compare** — slow — 3 days to give a plan.

New PM Xiaoli only read 5 product books, but each one **used 100 times**.

Xiaoli makes decisions: **mobilize 5 core methods** — fast — half a day for a plan — **the plan up 30% in 2 months**.

You make decisions: **mobilize 200 methods** — 3 days for a plan — **up 5% in 2 months**.

---

**3 years later**:

- You: **more and more books, newer and newer methodologies, things you make get more and more complex** — **don't get promoted**.
- Xiaoli: **just those 5 books, just those 5 methods, things you make get more and more "right"** — **promoted to VP**.

**Laozi would say: "the pursuit of learning increases daily" — you "pursue learning", you "increase daily" — but your "pursuit of the Dao" is "decrease daily" — Xiaoli "pursues the Dao", he "decreases daily" — he **damages** the "loads" from "pursuit of learning" — damages to "non-action" — he "through non-action nothing is left undone"**.

**第 48 章**: "为学日益, 为道日损"——为学日益——为道日损——"损之又损, 以至于无为——无为而无不为"。

两章是**"不出户+不窥牖+其出弥远其知弥少"+"为学日益+为道日损+损之又损=无为而无不为"**——

chapters.tension_en:
**Chapter 47**: "Without going out the door, know the world; without peeking through the window, see the way of heaven" — without going out — know the world — without peeking — see the way of heaven — "the further you go, the less you know".

**Chapter 48**: "Pursuit of learning is daily increase; pursuit of the Dao is daily decrease" — pursuit of learning daily increases — pursuit of the Dao daily decreases — "decrease and again decrease, until arriving at non-action — through non-action nothing is left undone".

Two chapters are **"without going out + without peeking + the further you go the less you know" + "pursuit of learning daily increases + pursuit of the Dao daily decreases + decrease and again decrease = through non-action nothing is left undone"** —

> **Chapter 47: without going out + without peeking + the further you go the less you know (without going out = know the world; the further you go = the less you know)**
> **Chapter 48: pursuit of learning daily increases + pursuit of the Dao daily decreases + decrease and again decrease = through non-action nothing is left undone (pursuit of learning = daily increase; pursuit of the Dao = daily decrease)**

- Chapter 47 teaches you "without going out + without peeking + the further you go the less you know"
- Chapter 48 teaches you "pursuit of learning daily increases + pursuit of the Dao daily decreases + decrease and again decrease = through non-action nothing is left undone"

**"Without going out + the further you go the less you know" + "pursuit of learning daily increases + pursuit of the Dao daily decreases = through non-action nothing is left undone" = less going out + decrease = you are in "Dao".**

chapters.original_en:
The sage has no fixed mind.
He takes the mind of the people as his mind.
To the good I am good.
To the not-good I am also good.
Thus the virtue of goodness.
To the trustworthy I am trustworthy.
